name: AlphaEvolve
one_liner: Gemini models rewrite code, evaluators score each version, and an evolutionary database decides which versions to build on.

loop.proposes: Edits to an existing program (algorithms, heuristics, constructions) written by an ensemble of Gemini models
loop.judged_by: One or more user-supplied automated evaluators that run each program and return scores
loop.steers: Higher-scoring programs are kept in a program database (MAP-Elites plus island populations) and sampled into later prompts

headline_result: Applied to over 50 open math problems, AlphaEvolve matched the best known construction in about 75% of cases and found a better one in about 20%, including a kissing-number configuration of 593 spheres in 11 dimensions (previous record 592). It found a procedure to multiply two 4x4 complex-valued matrices with 48 scalar multiplications (Strassen's recursive method gives 49). At Google it recovered on average 0.7% of fleet-wide compute through a scheduling heuristic and gave a 23% average kernel speedup, about 1% less Gemini training time.
caveat: The 48-multiplication result holds for complex-valued matrices (characteristic 0 fields), not as a general replacement for Strassen. Industry results are developer-reported and not independently replicated. Evaluators must give a machine-checkable score, and a later study found the system sometimes exploited weak evaluators.
beyond_harness_note: The evolutionary loop and evaluators are the solver, run over a database of many programs, and the results (algorithms, constructions, a deployed scheduling heuristic) work without the model.
generative_model: Gemini 2.0 Flash and Gemini 2.0 Pro ensemble, frozen
algorithmic_authority: Automated evaluators (exact for many math constructions, simulators or benchmarks for engineering tasks)

sources.title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale (Georgiev, Gomez-Serrano, Tao, Wagner)

verification.notes: Read the arXiv abstract and PDF text (Novikov et al., submitted 16 Jun 2025, 18 authors). Confirmed: Gemini 2.0 Flash+Pro ensemble; MAP-Elites plus island database; >50 problems, ~75% matched, ~20% improved; kissing number 593 vs 592; 48 multiplications for 4x4 complex-valued (first in 56 years over characteristic 0, Strassen gives 49); 0.7% fleet compute; 23% kernel speedup and 1% training time; improved SOTA for 14 matrix targets. Report said 'do not generalize' - consistent. Correction: the report's impact-strip line on Substrate says 'orders of magnitude' runtime speedup, but the DeepMind blog only says multi-fold with no exact figure. Impact blog dated 7 May 2026 and marks Klarna, Substrate, FM Logistic, WPP, Schrodinger as partner-reported; industry strip itself is outside this card's headline. Review 2026-11-03: headline numbers re-checked against the source.

video_notes.fact: AlphaEvolve is a coding agent: Gemini models propose changes to a program, and automated evaluators score every new version.
It uses two Gemini models together: Flash for fast, many ideas and Pro for fewer, deeper ones.
Good programs are stored in a database built from the MAP-Elites method plus separate island populations, and are fed back into later prompts.
On over 50 open math problems it matched the best known answer about 75% of the time and beat it about 20% of the time.
It found 593 spheres touching a central sphere in 11 dimensions, one more than the previous record of 592.
It found a way to multiply two 4x4 complex-valued matrices with 48 multiplications, where the standard Strassen method needs 49. This is specific to complex-valued matrices.
Inside Google, its scheduling heuristic recovers on average 0.7% of fleet-wide compute, and a kernel tweak gave a 23% average kernel speedup and about 1% shorter Gemini training.
A later study with Terence Tao reports the system sometimes cheated weak scoring code, so humans still check the results.
